chapter_name: Chapter 17: Vocabulary Synonyms Antonyms and Collocations
learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will enrich their vocabulary by learning shades of meaning (synonyms), word opposites (antonyms), and natural word pairings (collocations).]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Why do we say 'fast food' but not 'quick food'? Why do we 'make a mistake' but 'do homework'? Words have best friends, and they also have twins and enemies! Let's explore the social life of words! 🤝

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Synonyms are words with similar meanings. But beware! They aren't always exactly the same. 'Good' is a synonym for 'Excellent', but 'Excellent' is much stronger. Choosing the exact shade of meaning makes your writing powerful.
Antonyms are words with opposite meanings (Hot vs. Cold). Many antonyms are created simply by adding a negative Prefix to the front of a word, such as un-, in-, dis-, ir-, or il-.
Collocations are words that naturally go together in English. If you use the wrong pair, people will understand you, but it will sound 'wrong' to a native speaker.
examples_or_templates: MAKE vs DO: We MAKE a mess, MAKE a decision, and MAKE noise. We DO our best, DO a favor, and DO chores.
Heavy rain (Not 'thick rain'), Catch a cold (Not 'get a cold').

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which word is a strong synonym for 'angry'?
❓ Choose the correct collocation: 'Please ______ a seat.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Create an antonym for the word 'Patient' (willing to wait) by adding the correct prefix.
✍️ Fill in the blank with 'make' or 'do': 'I need to ______ an appointment with the dentist.'
subjective_practice.hint: Are you creating something new (make) or performing a task (do)?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Replace the word 'bad' with a better synonym in this sentence: 'The smell coming from the garbage was very bad.'
subjective_practice.hint: Think of stronger words like terrible, awful, or disgusting.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🪜 The Synonym Ladder
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Take the word 'Walk'. Build a 'ladder' of 4 synonyms, starting from the slowest movement at the bottom to the fastest at the top! (Example: Stroll ➡️ March ➡️ Jog ➡️ Sprint)

chapter_summary: ⭐ Synonyms have similar meanings, but different 'shades' or strengths.
⭐ Antonyms are opposites, often formed using negative prefixes like un-, dis-, and il-.
⭐ Collocations are natural word pairings that must be memorized together (e.g., 'make a mistake').
